name: Sukhoi Su-30MKI
overview_md:
The Sukhoi Su-30MKI is the heavyweight backbone of the Indian Air Force — a twin-engine, two-seat air-dominance fighter built in India by HAL under licence, and the most numerous and capable type in the IAF's frontline fleet. A heavily customised development of the Russian Su-30, the "MKI" (Modernizirovanniy Kommercheskiy Indiski) blends Russian airframe and engines with Israeli, French and Indian avionics into a uniquely Indian aircraft.

Its defining features are agility and reach. Canards and thrust-vectoring AL-31FP engines give it exceptional manoeuvrability, while two engines and large fuel capacity provide the range to patrol India's vast frontiers with both China and Pakistan. With more than 260 in service, it carries a deep and varied weapons load — and most significantly, it is the launch platform for the air-launched BrahMos-A supersonic cruise missile, giving India a long-range maritime- and land-strike capability from the air.

For an analyst, the Su-30MKI is the muscle of Indian airpower and a barometer of India's defence trajectory. An ambitious "Super Sukhoi" upgrade — adding an indigenous AESA radar (Virupaksha), new mission computers and weapons — aims to keep the fleet relevant into the 2040s. It sits alongside the smaller numbers of French Rafales and the indigenous Tejas, anchoring India's two-front airpower against a modernising PLA Air Force.

builder: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), under licence from Sukhoi

combat_history.event: Su-30MKIs flew air-defence sorties during the India–Pakistan Balakot crisis.
combat_history.significance: Front-line role in a live two-nation military confrontation.

modernization.description: Fleet-wide upgrade with indigenous AESA radar, mission systems and weapons.
modernization.impact: Keeps the IAF's most numerous fighter relevant for decades.

vulnerabilities.description: Large radar signature against modern stealth fighters and IADS.
vulnerabilities.context: Outmatched by 5th-gen types like the J-20 in a first-look fight.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: AESA and weapons upgrades; numbers and reach.

vulnerabilities.description: The fleet has faced serviceability and Russian-supply-chain challenges.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Air dominance and long-range strike across India's northern and maritime frontiers.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Operates with Rafale, MiG-29 and indigenous Tejas in the IAF.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The J-20 is a 5th-gen stealth fighter; the Su-30MKI is a highly agile 4th-gen with great range and the BrahMos.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: India's Flanker vs China's stealth fighter.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Both are advanced Flanker derivatives; the MKI is Indianised with Western avionics and the BrahMos.
The Rafale is a smaller, more modern omnirole fighter; the Su-30MKI provides mass and reach.

doctrine.role: Heavyweight air-dominance and long-range strike fighter — the backbone of the Indian Air Force.
doctrine.employment: Long-range patrols and BVR air combat; air-launched BrahMos for maritime and land strike.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Agility and reach via thrust-vectoring and twin engines, Indianised with multinational avionics.
doctrine.threat_context: Anchors India's two-front airpower against China's modernising PLAAF and Pakistan.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the J-20 (adversary), the Su-35 (cousin) and the Rafale (stablemate).
